precepts.text: Christ prays that the disciples may be one as we are one: one in spirit and speech, not one entity, or the disciples are one being too.
precepts.point: I and my Father are one is the one scripture the priest quotes; John 17 tells you what one means.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
The priest explaining the sign of the cross as three distinct persons of one essence never opens a Bible. The one scripture he leans on is John 10:30: “I and my Father are one.” That's all he has. But Christ says it again in John 17, and there he tells you what one means.

“And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are.” These are his disciples. If one means one being, one essence, then Christ and the disciples are all one being too. That's not what it's talking about. They are one because they speak the same things, say the same things, in the same spirit.

“Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us”. “And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one”. So are they all one entity? Do they form Voltron, do the fusion dance, become a Megazord? It's madness; it's ridiculous. One means one in spirit and speech, not one entity.

That is why they never bring out the Bible. The trinity was argued out over centuries of councils, borrowed from Greek philosophy, confusion upon confusion, and God is not the author of confusion. The Bible is plain: “to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.” Paul warned, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit”.

Herod was an Idumean, an Edomite, and this Edomite wanted favor with the Jews.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Christ said: “The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.” Who is he talking about? Rome. Remember, Herod was an Idumean, and Rome were Idumeans: they were the same race.

That thief stole the name. Their own book, written by Esau and not by a negro, says the Jews of today are of two types, the Sephardic and the Ashkenazi. Initially we were the Sephardim in Spain; when they conquered us and cast us out, Esau became the Sephardic ones. The Ashkenazi, 90 percent of the so-called Jews, came from the Khazars, and their own Jewish Encyclopedia says the Khazars are of Edomite stock, from the land of Edom. We had to find out whether they were Japheth or Esau, and their own sources answer it. We have second, third and fourth book sources, and the Bible is always our main source.

“Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” God calls Edom “the people of my curse”. If God hated you and your ancestors, you would want to hide that you are Esau. That is why they claim to be Israel, form the Anti-Defamation League, push hate crime laws, and infiltrate the churches. The thief came to steal, kill and destroy; Christ came that we might have life.

precepts.text: I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture. You want to get to the Most High? You enter in through Christ.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
The last part of John 14:6 is “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” By Christ we know the Father. He says it another way: “I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.”

He is that door. You want to get to the Most High? You have to enter in through Christ, and whoever enters by him shall be saved.

“and shall go in and out, and find pasture.” He shall go in and out and find pasture, and find that rest. The door is the only way in to the Father, and on the other side of it is the pasture and the rest the sheep are fed with. That is how the bread from heaven feeds a dying man: by coming through Christ.

precepts.text: Christ said, I and my Father are one. Is there a division between Christ and his Father? No, they are on one accord.
precepts.point: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord. We start with the order first. We as a body have to be one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this congregation: because we are one.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord.” One mind, one body: we start with the order first. The Lord our God is one Lord, and Christ shows what that oneness looks like: “I and my Father are one.”

Is there a division between Christ and his Father? No. They are on one accord. Two persons, the Father and the Son, and yet one, because the Son is in full agreement with the Father.

That is what we as a body have to be: one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this body, in this congregation: because we are one. Many of our people today have a social religion, more like a superstition, believing what society told them to do. We rely on the scriptures and believe on the Lord as it is written, and the scripture says the Lord is one and Christ is one with him.

precepts.text: The rock of our salvation is Christ. We are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand: to day if ye will hear his voice. The same thing Christ said in John 10: they shall hear my voice.
precepts.point: For all of us, there was a time that we heard this voice. We heard the word of God and it triggered us to repentance, to change. Something innate in us made us acknowledge the word of God by hearing his voice and changing our life.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Everything Christ and the apostles spoke was already spoken in what we call the Old Testament, and they used it to substantiate their points. So when Christ says of his other sheep, “they shall hear my voice”, the psalm already said it.

“O come, let us sing unto the Lord: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation.” The rock of our salvation is Christ. “For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. In his hand are the deep places of the earth”; “The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the Lord our maker.”

“For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice.” We are the sheep of his hand, and the condition is the same: if you will hear his voice. That is exactly what Christ said in John 10: “them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice.”

For all of us there was a time that we heard this voice. We heard the word of God, and it brought us to repentance, to change. Something innate in us made us acknowledge the word of God by hearing his voice and changing our life. That is how the sheep of his pasture are known.

precepts.text: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee: all twelve tribes. I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold. The same thing Christ was saying: them also I must bring, that there may be one fold and one shepherd.
precepts.point: For all of us, there was a time that we heard this voice. We heard the word of God and it triggered us to repentance, to change. Something innate in us made us acknowledge the word of God by hearing his voice and changing our life.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Christ said, “there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.” The fold he was speaking in was the Jews in Jerusalem, primarily Judah, Benjamin and Levi. The other sheep, not of that fold, were the rest of Israel, and he would gather the two nations, the southern and northern kingdoms, together under one shepherd, Jesus Christ.

Micah prophesied that one fold: “I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men.”

“all of thee” means all twelve tribes. That is the same thing Christ was saying: I have sheep that are not of this fold; them also I must bring, that there may be one fold and one shepherd. The prophecy was that all twelve tribes were going to be brought back together.

The beginning of it coming to fruition was when Christ came and began to teach, and his dying was the beginning of the twelve tribes being gathered back together. That is what his death was about: he was sent by his Father to gather the flock of Jacob into one fold.

precepts.text: Caiaphas prophesied that it was expedient one man die for the people, that the whole nation perish not; and not for that nation only, but that he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad. Even the evil high priest saw both kingdoms gathered.
precepts.point: I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice, and there shall be one fold and one shepherd. Christ is of Judah, so 'this fold' is the southern kingdom and the other sheep are the northern kingdom, brought in through Judah's teaching, fulfilling Hosea 1 and Ezekiel 37.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Christ said, “I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”. Christ is of Judah, so this fold is the southern kingdom, and the other sheep are the northern kingdom. “them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice”, through the teachings of Judah first, “and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd”: one head, one king, as Hosea 1 and Ezekiel 37 said.

The Lord moved even the high priest, as stupid and evil as he was, to see it too. “And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The whole nation is all of us, all twelve tribes; Christ did not die for one kingdom only.

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” The children of God scattered abroad are the ones Peter wrote to in 1 Peter 1: the northern kingdom. He gathered both kingdoms together as one.

So Caiaphas, who hated the Messiah, prophesied the same thing Christ said: other sheep not of this fold, brought into one fold. The builders were appointed to reject Christ, because by rejecting him they would have him killed, and by being killed he would grant the northern kingdom a chance to repent and be redeemed back into the fold.

precepts.text: Christ kept the feast of dedication in winter, not a December birthday.
precepts.point: Titus warns against Jewish fables and the commandments of men that turn from the truth.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
There is a winter holiday that Christ kept: “And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.” Read on: “And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch.” The feast of dedication is celebrated in the winter, and Christ was there at the feast in the wintertime.

So the holiday of the winter that Christ kept was the feast of dedication, not a December birthday. Christmas, December 25th and the birthday of Christ are fables and commandments of men, and people have turned their ears from the truth to follow them.

The same goes for the new year. The new year is in the spring, not the winter. Abib, or Aviv, means spring: the season when the young, tender barley ears first appear, marking the start of the religious new year around March or April in the Gregorian calendar, the time of the Passover and the firstfruits offering, signifying renewal and freedom from Egypt. They celebrate the new year in the winter. And if you see Israelite groups keeping Passover in February, or July, or June, there is something wrong. The truth is in the scriptures; the winter birthday and the winter new year are the fables they turned to.

precepts.text: I am the door of the sheep: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved. This is the way the sheep go through; this is how they get to the Most High: they come through Christ.
precepts.point: What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep. All that ever came before me are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them. I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture.”

This is the way the sheep go through. This is how they get to the Most High: they come through Christ. He is the one standing at the door of your spirit and knocking.

precepts.text: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
precepts.point: The northern and southern kingdoms are to be made one nation again under one king and one shepherd. The one king is Jesus Christ, called the throne of David because David ruled over all twelve tribes; David will be present but is not the king. The chief shepherd, the great shepherd, the good shepherd who lays down his life is Christ, and he gathers the elect from the four winds and brings them up out of the land.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
“I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.”

The one shepherd that Israel shall have is Christ. He is the good shepherd who lays down his life. He is the one king over the twelve tribes, called by David's name because he comes of David's line, and he is the shepherd who gathers the sheep back into one nation.

precepts.text: My sheep hear My voice and follow Me; we follow this Bible, and a stranger will they not follow but flee from him, leaving the strange doctrines alone.
precepts.point: Let my soul live, and it shall praise Thee, and let Thy judgments help me. I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek Thy servant, for I do not forget Thy commandments. The lost sheep is the house of Israel, the people who go astray and must seek the face of the Most High early and follow this Bible, fleeing the strange doctrines.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:” The lost sheep of the house of Israel hear his voice and follow him, and we follow this Bible. A stranger they will not follow but will flee from him, so we leave the strange doctrines alone.

That is the sheep David describes: gone astray, yet “I do not forget thy commandments”, longing for salvation, with the law as his delight and his tongue speaking of the word, “for all thy commandments are righteousness.”

precepts.text: The scripture cannot be broken, so what the Most High has spoken concerning the low tree exalted and the high tree brought down He will surely do.
precepts.point: If the Most High has declared it, it shall come to pass, for the scripture cannot be broken.

note.label: Ezekiel 17: The Riddle of the Two Eagles

precepts.why:
Christ says “the scripture cannot be broken”. What the Most High has spoken, He will do; He says so Himself at the end of this passage: “I the Lord have spoken and have done it.”

So the whole thing is sure. He Himself takes of the highest branch of the high cedar, crops off a tender twig and plants it “upon an high mountain and eminent”, in the mountain of the height of Israel. It brings forth boughs, bears fruit and becomes a goodly cedar under which “all fowl of every wing” dwell. All the trees of the field know that He has “brought down the high tree”, “exalted the low tree”, dried up the green tree and made the dry tree flourish.

If the Most High has declared it, it shall come to pass. The low tree exalted and the high tree brought down is not a maybe, because the scripture cannot be broken.
